text: Philip Coppens (October 24, 1930 – June 21, 2017) was a Dutch-born American chemist and crystallographer renowned for his work on charge density analysis using X-ray crystallography and his pioneering contributions to photocrystallography. Born in Amersfoort, Coppens earned his B.S. and Ph.D. degrees from the University of Amsterdam in 1954 and 1960, respectively, under the supervision of Carolina MacGillavry. In 1968, after holding positions at the Weizmann Institute and Brookhaven National Laboratory, he joined the chemistry department at the State University of New York at Buffalo, where he served as a SUNY Distinguished Professor and held the Henry M. Woodburn Chair of Chemistry. Among the three-dimensional structures he characterized is the nitroprusside ion. He was a corresponding member of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences since 1979 and a fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science from 1993. Coppens received the Gregori Aminoff Prize from the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in 1996, the Ewald Prize from the International Union of Crystallography in 2005, and the Kołos Medal in 2013.
